lessons.title: Cloud Computing Fundamentals
lessons.concept: Cloud computing delivers computing resources (servers, storage, databases, networking, software) over the internet on-demand, typically with pay-as-you-go pricing. It enables scalability, flexibility, and reduced need for owning/maintaining physical infrastructure.
lessons.formula: Key ideas: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service (common characteristics).
lessons.worked_example: Instead of buying and maintaining physical servers, a company can rent virtual machines or managed services from a cloud provider and scale capacity up or down based on demand.
mistakes: Assuming cloud means data is always stored on your local machine
Thinking cloud eliminates all security responsibilities (shared responsibility model applies)
Confusing cloud computing with just internet access
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Service Models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
lessons.concept: Cloud service models define the level of abstraction and responsibility. IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides virtualized infrastructure (VMs, storage, networks). PaaS (Platform as a Service) provides a platform/runtime for developing and deploying applications. SaaS (Software as a Service) delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet.
lessons.formula: Responsibility shifts: IaaS -> more user control of OS/apps; PaaS -> manage app/data, provider manages platform; SaaS -> provider manages most layers, user uses software.
lessons.worked_example: IaaS: virtual machines. PaaS: managed app hosting platform. SaaS: email or CRM applications accessed via browser.
mistakes: Assuming SaaS users manage underlying servers
Thinking one model fits all use cases
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Deployment Models and Benefits/Considerations
lessons.concept: Deployment models include public cloud (shared infrastructure, provider-managed), private cloud (dedicated to one organization), hybrid cloud (combination), and multi-cloud (multiple providers). Benefits include scalability and cost flexibility; considerations include security, compliance, latency, and vendor lock-in.
lessons.formula: Public: shared, scalable. Private: dedicated/control. Hybrid: mix of environments. Multi-cloud: multiple cloud providers.
lessons.worked_example: A hybrid setup may keep sensitive data in a private environment while using public cloud for scalable web workloads.
mistakes: Assuming public cloud is always insecure or always secure without context
